topic: Machines can now guess what you are looking at from brain scans
subject: future

facts.claim: Machine-learning models can predict the contents of visual imagery during the sleep-onset period by discovering links between human functional magnetic resonance imaging patterns and verbal reports.
facts.quote: Here we present a neural decoding approach in which machine-learning models predict the contents of visual imagery during the sleep-onset period, given measured brain activity, by discovering links between human functional magnetic resonance imaging patterns and verbal reports

facts.claim: A brain decoding technique combined with deep neural network representations can reconstruct illusory percepts as images from brain activity.
facts.quote: Here, we leverage a brain decoding technique combined with deep neural network (DNN) representations to reconstruct illusory percepts as images from brain activity.

facts.claim: The DBDM model achieved Inception, CLIP and SwAV distances of 0.611, 0.225 and 0.405, respectively, when reconstructing semantic details of original images from fMRI patterns.
facts.quote: In particular, the best performance is achieved by DBDM in reconstructing the semantic details of the original image; the Inception, CLIP and SwAV distances are 0. 611, 0. 225 and 0. 405, respectively.

facts.claim: A two-stage framework called Brain-Diffuser can reconstruct images that capture low-level properties and overall layout from fMRI signals.
facts.quote: In the first stage, starting from fMRI signals, we reconstruct images that capture low-level properties and overall layout using a VDVAE (Very Deep Variational Autoencoder) model.

facts.claim: The NeuralDiffuser model provides detailed cues in the form of gradients to achieve both semantic coherence and detail fidelity when reconstructing visual stimuli.
facts.quote: This extension of the bottom-up process for diffusion models achieves both semantic coherence and detail fidelity when reconstructing visual stimuli.

research.angle: Generative models can reconstruct natural images, semantic details, and even subjective experiences like dreams or illusions from fMRI brain activity.
research.verdict: Multiple studies demonstrate that diffusion models and deep neural networks can successfully decode fMRI signals into visual reconstructions ranging from low-level layouts to complex semantic details.
research.caveat: The research focuses on reconstructing visual stimuli and experiences rather than real-time, high-fidelity visual streaming.
